name: SFX Kit
description: Selección de 51 sonidos del SFX Kit de Wyzowl (CC0) para anuncios tipo reel. Mismo formato que sounds.json del kit completo.
credit: Not required. If you'd like to: "SFX Kit by Wyzowl" (https://github.com/wyzowl/sfx-kit).

how_to_use.find: GUIDE.md lists common on-screen moments with sounds made for them. A sound's use_for, avoid_for and tags say what it suits; its variant how it differs from its siblings (softer or harder, lighter or heavier, shorter or longer); fits_seconds the length of moment it fits.
how_to_use.place: Start every sound at (the moment it should meet) − sync.at. sync.at already points at the part of the sound that should meet the moment (the hit, the start of a gesture, a sequence's first event even when a later one is louder, the till's bell), so this one rule holds for every sound. sync.meets says what kind of moment that is (instant, action-start, move-peak, arrival or release) and sync.how says it in words; where it says to start a sound with an action, its sync point (where it becomes audible) meets the action's first frame. If you change a sound's rate, divide its times by the rate. If a start falls before 0, start at 0 and trim that much off the sound's beginning.
how_to_use.fit: span_seconds is the length of moment a sound fits at rate 1, so the rate that fits a moment exactly is span_seconds ÷ its length, within adapt.rate (fits_seconds is that range; a whoosh has no span, and its fits_seconds are the lengths of move it suits). A sound that runs with an action can lose its end, and a build that ends on its sync point its start; to drop a later part, cut just before its time in parts. Trims are in the file's own seconds (after a rate change, a trim of t is t ÷ rate on the timeline). The files start and end on silence, so a cut part-way through a sound needs a short fade (10 to 50 ms, or 300 ms or more for a long tail).
how_to_use.levels: Gains are relative to each file as it is (0 dB). Every file sits on one loudness scale (level.lufs is its loudest 150 ms), so the sounds are level with each other as they are, and a category's intensities differ in level on purpose. At 0 dB a medium effect's loudest moment is about −20.5 LUFS, a few dB under a voiceover mixed to about −16 LUFS integrated. under_voiceover_db is how far a sound comes down wherever its body (timing.onset to timing.body_end) overlaps speech, for the voice to stay clear over it. A sound whose avoid_for starts 'On top of speech' masks or competes with a voice even when it's lowered.
how_to_use.tuning: The tuned sounds are in C major, so they agree with each other: most only on its pentatonic notes (tuning: C major pentatonic), which also sit with music in G or F major, or in A, E or D minor. Sounds with adapt.rate [1, 1] keep their rate: the tuned ones, and a few whose pitch must stay true.

loudness.measure: level.lufs is the loudest 150 ms of the sound, K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770), in LUFS. Mono sounds are measured as if played on both speakers.
loudness.tiers: Each category sets the levels of its intensities on this one scale, so soft and hard stay apart and categories sit together. Bass-heavy sounds feel louder than they measure: the scale weighs low frequencies lightly.

sounds.name: Whoosh, fast and soft
sounds.description: A quick, gentle puff of air with a soft edge and no weight.
use_for: Small icons or text sliding in
Tooltips, chips and small UI panels moving
List items arriving one after another (at a lower gain)

sync.how: Ease-in-out: put the sync point at the middle of the move. Ease-out (fast start, slowing to a stop): about a quarter of the way in. Ease-in (slow start, fast exit): about three quarters of the way in.

adapt.notes: To fit a move up to about 15% shorter or 20% longer, play it faster or slower (its pitch moves with it); beyond that, use the next speed. Adjust level with gain, but for a clearly softer or harder sound use the other intensity rather than a big gain change.

pairs_with.how: Something landing: the whoosh on the move (its sync point at the move's fastest point) and the impact on the frame it lands. A whoosh that suits the move's length dies away just before the landing; use one a step softer than the impact.
Something arriving and appearing: the whoosh during the move, the pop as it lands, at a lower gain than the whoosh.
A reveal: the whoosh into the reveal, the shimmer starting at the whoosh's sync point.

sounds.name: Swish, medium
sounds.description: A quick, clean swish through the air, with a little whistle.
use_for: Text, icons or arrows flicked into place
Quick cuts, wipes and whip transitions
A line or pointer sweeping across

sync.how: Put the sync point where the move is fastest: the middle of an ease-in-out move.

adapt.notes: To fit a quicker or slower move, change the rate a little (its pitch moves with it); for a much longer move, use a whoosh.

pairs_with.how: Something flicked in and appearing: the swish, then a small pop as it lands.

sounds.name: Zip in, medium
sounds.description: A quick zip in: rising to a stop.
use_for: Icons, labels or badges zipping in and stopping
A line drawing to its end
Arrows reaching a target (add a light impact)

sync.how: Put the sync point (near the end) on the frame it arrives and stops: start = arrival − sync.at.

adapt.notes: To fit a quicker or slower move, change the rate a little (its pitch moves with it); for a much longer move, use a whoosh.

pairs_with.how: Something arriving with weight: the zip in, with a light impact on its sync point.

sounds.name: Zip out, medium
sounds.description: A quick zip out: off it goes, falling away.
use_for: Something sent flying: a message, a file

sync.how: Put the sync point (right at its start) on the frame the move begins.

adapt.notes: To fit a quicker or slower move, change the rate a little (its pitch moves with it); for a much longer move, use a whoosh.

pairs_with.how: Something knocked away: a light impact, then the zip out starting with it.

sounds.name: Reverse whoosh, short and soft
sounds.description: A short soft reverse whoosh: air drawn in, building to a sudden stop.
use_for: Something collapsing or shrinking into a point
The build into a hard cut, a hit or a reveal
An element pulled back into a button or icon
avoid_for: Moments that should land softly (it stops dead)

sync.how: Place it so its end (the sync point) lands on the moment of collapse, the cut or the hit: start = that moment − sync.at.

adapt.notes: For other lengths, pick the nearest one and trim its quiet start rather than changing the rate.

pairs_with.how: A pull into a hit: the reverse whoosh, its end on the impact's sync point.
A big moment: the reverse whoosh into a boom starting on its sync point.
Something sucked into a point and gone: the reverse whoosh with a small pop out at its end, at −6 dB.

sounds.character: soft, airy pull to a stop

sounds.name: Riser, 1 s, soft
sounds.description: A 1-second soft, airy rise that builds to its peak at the end.
use_for: Building up to a reveal: a logo, a product, a big number
A short lift before something appears
avoid_for: Reveals that land before the rise ends: the peak is at its end

sync.how: Place it so its end (the sync point) lands on the reveal: start = reveal − sync.at.

adapt.notes: For other lengths, change the rate a little (its pitch moves with it), or take the next longer one and trim its quiet start (risers) or its quiet end (fallers).

pairs_with.how: A reveal with weight: the rise into an impact on the reveal frame.
A bright reveal: the rise into a shimmer starting at its sync point.
A big reveal: the rise into a boom on the reveal frame.

sounds.name: Zoom in

sounds.name: Impact, deep, on a hard surface
sounds.description: A deep, hard hit: a crisp crack over a heavy, rumbling low end.
use_for: Big, weighty landings with real bass
A title or object slamming down
Moments that need to be felt
avoid_for: On top of speech: the bass masks it

sync.how: Put the sync point (the moment of contact) exactly where the thing lands: usually the last frame of its move, or the first frame it's at rest.

adapt.notes: Small rate changes only: faster sounds lighter and slower heavier, so for a different weight use the next weight instead.

pairs_with.how: A move into a landing: the whoosh on the move (its sync point at the move's fastest point), the impact on the frame it lands. Use a whoosh one step softer than the impact.
Something landing and appearing: the impact for the weight, a small pop on top at about −6 dB.

sounds.name: Boom hit, medium
sounds.description: A deep, rounded boom with a warm hall.
use_for: A title card or logo landing with weight
A big statement or a key number
avoid_for: On top of speech: its low end masks it

sync.how: Sync point on the frame of the reveal or the landing (it's at the very start). Leave the tail to ring out: the hall is part of it.

adapt.notes: Slower sounds deeper and longer; faster lighter. For a shorter boom, fade the tail out over 300 ms or more rather than cutting it.

pairs_with.how: A built-up reveal: the riser's end on the boom's sync point.
A pull into a big moment: the reverse whoosh's stop on the boom's sync point.
A big, bright reveal: the boom with a shimmer starting with it at −4 dB.

sounds.name: Cinematic drum hit, big

sync.how: Sync point on the frame of the hit: the title landing, the cut, the reveal. Let the hall ring out.

adapt.notes: Slower sounds bigger and deeper; faster tighter. To shorten one, fade its tail over 500 ms or more.

pairs_with.how: A pull into the hit: the reverse whoosh's stop on the hit's sync point.
A built-up hit: a strong riser whose end meets the hit.

sounds.name: Pop in, small
sounds.description: A tiny, bright pop that lifts as it appears.
use_for: Elements appearing or scaling up into view
Icons, badges and stickers popping in
avoid_for: Things leaving the screen (use pop out)

sync.how: Put the sync point where the element reaches full size (pop in, bubble) or where it vanishes (pop out). For a scale-up with overshoot, the sync point at the peak of the overshoot.

adapt.notes: Rate changes shift the pitch: a little faster for a smaller element, a little slower for a bigger one.

pairs_with.how: Something flying in and appearing: the whoosh during the move, the pop at its end, about 3 dB under the whoosh.
A message or badge appearing: the pop as it appears, the notification tone right after (40–80 ms).

sounds.name: Logo sting, minimal, short
sounds.description: A minimal sting: two kalimba notes, rising.
use_for: Calm films where a big sting would jar
A logo that appears at once
avoid_for: Mid-film transitions: a sting says 'ending' or 'brand moment'
On top of speech: time its hit to a pause in the voice

sync.how: Put the sync point (the hit) on the frame the logo appears or lands: start = that frame − sync.at. In a long sting the hit comes about a second in, after a lead-in, so the sound starts before the logo does.

adapt.notes: Don't change the rate: it detunes the notes. To shorten one, fade its tail over 300 ms or more.

pairs_with.how: A logo flying in: a soft whoosh on its move (its sync point at the move's fastest point) and the sting's hit on the frame it lands; keep the whoosh 3 dB under the sting.

avoid_for: Mid-film transitions: a sting says 'ending' or 'brand moment'
On top of speech: time its hit to a pause in the voice

sync.how: Put the sync point (the hit) on the frame the logo appears or lands: start = that frame − sync.at. In a long sting the hit comes about a second in, after a lead-in, so the sound starts before the logo does.

adapt.notes: Don't change the rate: it detunes the notes. To shorten one, fade its tail over 300 ms or more.

pairs_with.how: A logo flying in: a soft whoosh on its move (its sync point at the move's fastest point) and the sting's hit on the frame it lands; keep the whoosh 3 dB under the sting.

sounds.name: Clock ticking
sounds.description: A clock ticking: tick, tock, once a second.
avoid_for: Moments that need no sense of time

sync.how: Start it with the scene: it ticks once a second from its very start. Loop it for longer.

adapt.notes: Small rate changes only; loop the ticking for longer scenes.

pairs_with.how: Time's up with a result: the timer, then a success or failure 200 ms after.

sounds.name: 3-2-1 countdown
sounds.description: A countdown: three beeps a second apart, then a higher beep on go.
avoid_for: Moments that need no sense of time

sync.how: The beeps are at 0, 1 and 2 s and go at 3 s: line the first up with the 3 on screen.

adapt.notes: Don't change the rate: the beeps are a second apart. For a quicker count, use single beeps from it.

pairs_with.how: Time's up with a result: the timer, then a success or failure 200 ms after.

sounds.name: Glitch, clear
sounds.description: A crisp little glitch, stepping in pitch.
avoid_for: Natural, physical subjects (use foley, impacts or whooshes)

sync.how: Sync point on the frame it happens.

adapt.notes: Rate changes shift the pitch; small changes are fine.

pairs_with.how: A process that finishes: the process run, then a success or error notification at its end.
A digital transition: a soft whoosh with a glitch at its sync point, −6 dB.

sounds.name: Count-up, medium
sounds.description: A count-up of about 1.2 seconds: ticks that speed up and settle.
use_for: A statistic counting up to its value
A price or total adding up
avoid_for: Counts much longer than the run: use the next length or a count tick per step

sync.how: Start it with the count-up and match its length; the ticks ease in and out like the number. Put a number-land at the end.

adapt.notes: Pick the nearest length, then adjust the rate a little to fit.

pairs_with.how: A count-up and its finish: the count-up run, then the number-land on the final value.
A standout figure: the number-land with a short soft shimmer starting with it.

sounds.name: Number landing
sounds.description: A woody knock with a small, bright ping: a number landing.
use_for: The final number of a count-up landing
avoid_for: Things that aren't data (use whooshes, pops or shimmers)

sync.how: Sync point on the frame the final number appears.

adapt.notes: Small rate changes only.

pairs_with.how: A count-up and its finish: the count-up run, then the number-land on the final value.
A standout figure: the number-land with a short soft shimmer starting with it.

sounds.name: Tap, soft
sounds.description: A soft fingertip tap on glass.
use_for: A finger tapping a card or tile
Selecting an item on a phone screen
avoid_for: Moments that need to be noticed over music

sync.how: Put the sync point on the frame the press lands.

adapt.notes: Rate changes shift the pitch a little: faster sounds lighter, slower heavier.

pairs_with.how: A button that confirms something: the click first, the notification tone 60–120 ms later.
A physical switch on screen: the click with a mechanical switch at −6 dB.

sounds.name: Button click, medium
sounds.description: A clean, crisp button click.

sync.how: Put the sync point on the frame the press lands.

adapt.notes: Rate changes shift the pitch a little: faster sounds lighter, slower heavier.

pairs_with.how: A button that confirms something: the click first, the notification tone 60–120 ms later.
A physical switch on screen: the click with a mechanical switch at −6 dB.

sounds.name: Step 1 of 5
sounds.description: Step 1 of 5: a soft marimba note (C), each one higher.
use_for: Words, lines or list items appearing one by one: step 1 for the first, 2 for the second…
Bullet points and checklists building up
Icons or cards appearing in a row
avoid_for: Items appearing all at once (use a single pop)
Lists longer than five: there are five steps

sync.how: Sync point on the frame each item appears; use the steps in order.

adapt.notes: Don't change the rate: it detunes the note.

pairs_with.how: Items popping in: the pop for each item and its step on top at −3 dB.

sounds.name: Error, soft
sounds.description: A soft, falling two-note marimba: something's not right, gently.
use_for: A failed action or a wrong input
avoid_for: Moments that must cut through loud music (use clear)

sync.how: Sync point on the frame the notification, tick or message appears.

adapt.notes: Don't change the rate: it detunes the notes.

pairs_with.how: A badge or bubble appearing: the pop as it appears, the notification 40–80 ms after.
A button that confirms: the click first, the notification 60–120 ms after.
